beats.narration_text: Hello, I'm Vineet S.. Ask what a product manager does, and you hear: decides what to build. In AI that is still true, but the thing being built is wrong some of the time, by design. Let's take the role apart.

props.command: What does a product manager actually do when the product is an AI model?
output: Same craft as any PM: user, problem, priorities
Shipping is the start of the learning

beats.narration_text: An AI product manager owns a product that is sometimes wrong, then makes it safe to rely on. Same craft as any product manager, but quality, data and trust stop being side concerns. They become the job.

props.text:
An AI product manager
ships a model, then
hopes it works.

beats.narration_text: Here is the shape of the job, layer by layer. First, the problem: is AI even the right tool? Then data and the model: what it learns from, and whether to build, buy, or call an API. Then evaluation, where you decide what good enough means. And on top, trust.

layers.title: Problem
layers.sub: Is AI the right tool at all?

layers.title: Data and model
layers.sub: What it learns from; build, buy, or call an API

beats.narration_text: None of this happens alone. The AI product manager sits between data scientists who build the model, engineers who ship it, designers who shape how it speaks, legal and privacy teams who set limits, and domain experts who know when an answer is wrong. The real skill is translation.

props.caption: The AI PM translates between all of them

beats.narration_text: First responsibility: define good before anyone builds. An ordinary spec says the button does this. An AI spec says: on a hundred real cases, answers must be right most of the time, and never do these harmful things. That test set is the contract.

props.arcCaption: The PM turns inputs into a measurable spec
props.settleLine: The test set is the contract

beats.narration_text: Launch is not the finish. Models drift as the world changes, so the AI product manager watches quality over time, gathers feedback, decides when to retrain or adjust, and keeps a human override ready. Shipping is where the learning starts.

layers.title: Release small, monitor
layers.sub: A limited group first; drift is expected

beats.narration_text: The most senior move is saying no. If fixed rules work, if one wrong answer is catastrophic, if the data does not exist, or if every decision must be explained exactly, AI may be the wrong tool. A good AI product manager kills ideas early.

So, the AI product manager. Owns a product that is sometimes wrong. Defines good with tests before building. Translates between data, engineering, design and legal. Keeps watching after launch. And knows when not to use AI at all.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. I am a product manager. Pick one feature we could build with AI. Write a one-page spec: the user problem, the data we would need, three test cases with expected answers, two things it must never do, and one metric to watch after launch. Then argue against building it. That last sentence is the point. A spec that survives its own best argument is worth building. Look at the three test cases Claude writes: if you cannot tell a right answer from a wrong one, the feature is not ready. Pause here, and run it on your own product.
